data.body_html:
If you want to explore the Costa del Sol from the water without a boating licence, Marbella boat rental no license prices 2032 start from just €749 for 2 hours. Spain’s maritime law allows vessels up to 12.5 metres to be chartered without a licence, as long as a qualified skipper is on board. Our fleet includes 8 boats in this category, all departing from Puerto Banús, with prices that include fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. This guide breaks down the real costs, boat options, and what you get for your money – no fluff, just facts.

Why You Don’t Need a Licence for Boats Under 12.5m

Spanish regulations (Real Decreto 875/2014) state that recreational vessels under 12.5 metres in length can be operated by anyone without a specific boating licence, provided a licensed skipper is present. All our no-licence charters include a professional skipper who handles navigation, docking, and safety. You can relax, swim, or even take the wheel under supervision – but the skipper remains legally responsible. This setup is standard across Marbella and ensures full insurance cover.

Full Fleet: No-Licence Boats Available in 2032

Beyond the table above, we also offer these no-licence boats (all under 12.5m):

  • Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) – ideal for couples or small families
  • Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) – compact bowrider for day trips
  • Red Tide (11m, 6 pax) – sporty open boat
  • Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) – classic fun on the water

All depart from Puerto Banús. The skipper will meet you at the boat 15 minutes before departure. You can also arrange pickup from Marbella Marina or Cabopino on request.

What’s Included in Every No-Licence Charter

Our prices are all-inclusive – no hidden extras. Here’s exactly what you get:

  • Licensed skipper – professional and English-speaking
  • Fuel – enough for the full charter duration
  • Drinks – water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks – crisps, nuts, fruit
  • Insurance – full liability and passenger cover
  • Safety equipment – life jackets, flares, first aid
  • Spanish VAT (21%) – included, no surprises

You are welcome to bring your own food and extra drinks on board. The boat has a cooler and ice.

Where Can You Go on a No-Licence Charter?

From Puerto Banús, you can cruise east towards Marbella’s Golden Mile and La Concha mountain views, or west to the secluded Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés coves. Popular stops include the sandbanks off Cabopino, the chic beach clubs of Estepona, and the marina at Sotogrande. Your skipper knows the best spots for swimming, snorkelling, and lunch. A 4-hour charter is enough to reach Cabopino and back; 8 hours lets you explore as far as Estepona.

How to Book Your No-Licence Boat Rental for 2032

Booking is straightforward. Send us a WhatsApp message with your preferred boat, date, duration, and number of guests. We’ll confirm availability and send a secure payment link. A 50% deposit holds the booking; the balance is due on the day. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks ahead during July and August. For last-minute availability, check our Marbella boat rental hub.

Compare No-Licence vs. Larger Yacht Charters

If your group is larger than 11 people, or you want a bigger boat like the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax), a licence is technically required – but our skipper handles it. Those larger charters start at €4,719 for 4 hours (with a free jet ski). For smaller groups on a budget, no-licence boats offer the best value. See our full fleet for all options.
